content.text: FCY's operations function needs a register of how the firm settles trades with each counterparty, per currency — standing settlement instructions. One instruction records the payment mechanics (bank transfer, custody account or cash sweep) and the operational contacts to involve. The spec sits on the house side of the CDM boundary (FCY standing rules R11): CDM attaches standing settlement instructions to
, not the payment rails, so this register is an FCY extension labelled as such per FCY standing rule R9. The spec also carries the
register the instructions' counterparty reference targets — no such entity exists in the deployment, so it is specified here rather than cited as an external dependency.
entity with a draft → active → retired lifecycle.
The one-active-instruction-per-counterparty-and-currency rule, the effectiveFrom/effectiveTo ordering rule, and the exclusion of retired instructions from new trades.
register the counterparty reference targets — minimal (name, LEI), added at the author's request because no legal-entity entity exists in the deployment.
Payment rails / SWIFT–RTGS connectivity — the company corpus places these outside the modelled scope.
Changes to the trade booking flow beyond excluding retired instructions from selection.
Legal-entity onboarding workflow (KYC, approvals) — the register here is a bare reference target, not an onboarding process.
An operations user creates a draft instruction for a counterparty and currency, fills in the method (one of the three subtypes) and any contacts, and activates it.

if another instruction for the same counterparty and currency is already active, activation is refused and the conflicting instruction is named. Later the instruction is retired; from then on it no longer appears when a new trade's settlement instruction is chosen, while existing trades keep pointing at it.
